title: Laws of falling bodies (পড়ন্ত বস্তুর সূত্র)
placement: Book pages 48–49, topic 2.8: পড়ন্ত বস্তুর সূত্র (Laws of Falling Bodies). Next to Galileo's three laws and the paper-and-stone paragraph.
description: The book's own experiment in 3D (pages 48–49, 2.8): two clear tubes of the same height, one with air (বাতাস আছে) and one emptied (বাতাসহীন), each with a small stone and a piece of paper at rest at the same height, on the teacher's desk before the blackboard (the vacuum pump that emptied the right tube beside it). Press the red button on the release box (or a tube's top, or ছেড়ে দাও): all four fall at once, shown 8 times slower. In air the stone lands first (0.3 s) and the paper flutters down far behind (0.51 s); without air the stone and the paper land together (0.3 s): the first law. In the empty tube the bodies leave a faint picture every 0.1 s with a dashed line across the centimetre scale and a velocity arrow; the panel's table shows v = gt and h = ½gt² at 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 s, with the ratios 1 : 2 : 3 and 1 : 4 : 9 and the book's second and third laws (v ∝ t, h ∝ t²) and equations. Step 0.1 s at a time, or crumple the paper, an extra test the book doesn't do (the same mass, less air hindrance: it then falls almost with the stone even in air). Test tab: 5 questions (where the hidden paper is when the stone is at the 0.2 s line, why the paper lags in air, v and h from the equations or the picture, the ratio of distances or velocities, does the time depend on mass). Units: the book's SI symbols. Phone-first, Bangla.

params.name: t
params.label: Time after the release (paused)
